subject: geography
title: Rainforest Layers and Wildlife
welcome_lead: Climb the rainforest from floor to sky! Each layer has its own species and rhythms.
meta_desc: KS3 Geography adventure on rainforest layers and biodiversity.
final_note: Brilliant! You can now describe the four rainforest layers.

concepts.def: Tallest trees poking above the canopy.
Thick layer of treetops, most life lives here.
Shaded layer below canopy with shrubs.
Variety of plant and animal species.
Huge tree roots that support tall trunks.

walkthroughs.body_html:
• Emergent: giant trees up to 60m.
  • Canopy: dense leaves around 30m, most species live here.
  • Understorey: dim, with vines.
  • Forest floor: only 2% sunlight, fast decay.
Rainforests cover only 6% of Earth's land but host over half of all species! Toucans, jaguars, sloths, poison frogs and millions of insects all live here.
Tall trees grow buttress roots for support. Sloths move slowly to save energy. Frogs use bright colours as warnings.
